messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] SLO breach detected for Aurora Enterprise (VPC: ae-prod-eu) in eu-west-1 — p99 latency > SLO for 2 consecutive mins. Pager: oncall-sre.
oncall-sre: acknowledged. Paging rotation and starting war-room.
oncall-sre: quick triage: spike started ~11:02 UTC. p95 ~1.8s (baseline 400ms), p99 ~4.8s (baseline 2.3s). Error rates steady. Appears localized to Aurora's dedicated pool (dedicated-pool-aurora-eu1).
maria_account: oncall — immediate customer comms? They are in active support plan.
emily_support: I'll draft a terse customer update. Suggested: "We're investigating latency spikes affecting your eu-west-1 traffic; mitigation in progress; intermittent elevated p99. Next update in 15m." ok?
raj_devops: adding early notes — host CPU and GPU queue depth increased on pool nodes 7-10. Suspect bursty tenant causing KV cache churn. Will attempt tenant isolation first.
oncall-sre: plan: 1) isolate suspected noisy tenant (evict infra sessions) 2) scale dedicated pool + burst to 2x 3) route 10% traffic to eu-north fallback 4) warm prefixes. Executing eviction now.
raj_devops: running eviction command:
```
rctl pool evict --pool dedicated-pool-aurora-eu1 --tenant ae-tenant-42 --grace 30s
```
raj_devops: eviction completed, logs show connections dropping / reattaching. :white_check_mark: 
dmitri_infra: noticed KV cache miss rate jumped 3x at spike. Warming top prefixes (api/v1/complete) with a small script.
```
for p in $(cat top-prefixes.txt); do rctl cache warm --pool dedicated-pool-aurora-eu1 --prefix "$p" & done
```
ops-bot: Runbook pointer: incidents/tenant-noise-eviction.md — recommended throttle after eviction if issues persist.
raj_devops: scaled pool: 8 -> 16 nodes, autoscale applied. CPU queue depth improving.
oncall-sre: enabling region fallback routing (10%) to eu-north:
```
routingctl weight set --route ae-prod-eu --region eu-north --weight 10
```
oncall-sre: immediate impact: p99 dropped from 4.8s -> 2.1s at 11:14 UTC. Still above baseline but improving. Continuing to monitor. :eyes: 
maria_account: customer facing note (please edit): "We detected higher-than-normal latency for requests served from eu-west-1. We've isolated the noisy tenant, added capacity, and routed a portion of traffic to eu-north; performance is improving. We'll follow up with a full RCA and mitigation steps."
emily_support: will send now and open a support case thread. adding CC to account exec.
tim_pm: what's the rollback risk? if scaling doesn't help, do we force-fallback 100% to eu-north? cost/latency tradeoff?
oncall-sre: fallback 100% is possible but needs approval from PM/Account exec. For now keep at 10%, continue warming and letting cache stabilize. If p99 > 3s for next 10m, escalate to 50%.
maria_account: I'll ask the execs and get a quick sign-off.
oncall-sre: current action items: monitoring, prefix warm, keep eviction in place, pause non-critical background jobs for Aurora, update customer in 15m. Next check 11:20 UTC.
incident-bot: Incident status: active -> mitigation in progress. Incident channel: #inc-1725001234 (automatically created). Pager duty: oncall-sre remains primary. Reminder to log timeline in postmortem template. :warning:
